about.compat.1: What the mod does in this room (no mod roles): welcome and guide lines, chat auto-translation (into a foreign player's language too), the post-game result list (leavers included), keeping the room from timing out, Aegis anti-cheat (players doing impossible things are removed at once)
about.compat.1.notr: What the mod does in this room (no mod roles): welcome and guide lines, the post-game result list (leavers included), keeping the room from timing out, Aegis anti-cheat (players doing impossible things are removed at once). Chat is not translated
about.compat.2: The game itself is normal Among Us: usual roles as set, no mod roles or special rules
about.roles: PocketRoles: a host-only role mod; players install nothing; Aegis anti-cheat running. /cmd r lists the roles, /cmd n shows yours

opt.tip.anticheat.endgame: Unregistered rooms: when a player is removed mid-match for an impossible action (e.g. a kill by a role that cannot kill), the match ends at once, like the haison. The host returns by itself, the others with Play Again; then all are told why, with no name. Not for actions that change nothing (an impostor's task) or possible lag. Once per match, 3 times an hour. Needs 'Remove cheaters automatically'.

opt.tip.anticheat: In unregistered rooms, spots actions vanilla Among Us never produces (kills, vents, abilities, tasks by roles that cannot, alive chat outside meetings...) and shows them on the host's screen. /ac lists them.
opt.tip.anticheat.announce: When the anti-cheat removes someone, one public chat line says who and why.
opt.tip.anticheat.autoreport: Off by default (nobody is reported automatically). When on, Among Us's own player report (cheating) is sent before a removal for a certain detection: at most once per player every 30 days and 5 an hour. /opt anticheat.autoreport on also turns it on. Even while off, /aegis report <name> reports one player. A report cannot be taken back (a spoofing cheater could in theory frame someone).
opt.tip.anticheat.banladder: Players removed for a certain detection (a kill by a role that cannot...) are banned from every lobby you host: 30 days the first time, 180 days the second, permanent from the third. /aegis unban lifts one (the count is kept for a year after a ban ends). An evidence record is kept. Off: a ban for that room only. A spoofing cheater could in theory frame someone: check appeals against the evidence record.
opt.tip.anticheat.callout: In unregistered rooms: when a living crewmate names, in a meeting, impostors that have done nothing yet, the host alone is told (a sign of a role-seeing cheat; nobody is removed). Also someone who, game after game, votes for such impostors in meetings with no clue yet. While the host is a living crewmate it waits until the host dies or the game ends.
opt.tip.anticheat.jitter: Moves the Aegis limits (speed multiplier, chat flood count and seconds...) up or down at random within this percentage for every lobby, so a cheater cannot sit just under the published values (limits that can remove a player get at most half of it toward stricter). Only the host sees the drawn values (/ac rules lobby and the log). 0 = off. Default 10.
opt.tip.anticheat.kick: Removes (with a ban for this room) on the first certain detection (kill / vent / ability / task) or the second alive chat outside a meeting. VIP and above are exempt.
opt.tip.anticheat.remoterules: Takes the numbers Aegis judges with (chat flood count, speed multiplier...) and the rule levels from the definitions file on GitHub, so false positives and loopholes get fixed without a mod update (rule levels only get more lenient; the numbers move either way within fixed ranges). Off: built-in numbers and NG words, no shared bans; but changes that make a rule stop removing players (notice only / off), the required version and the list of erase requests are still received. /ac rules shows them.
opt.tip.anticheat.sharedbans: When someone on the shared ban list of the signed Aegis definitions file joins, they are told they cannot join (in unregistered rooms: one public line without a name) and removed 30 s later, at once on a cheat detection, an NG word, a chat flood or a game start (back in the same lobby: removed at once with a ban for that room). The list holds no names and no friend codes, only a hash of the PUID, which cannot be guessed back. VIP and above are exempt.

role.arsonist.desc: Neutral. Your kill button douses instead of killing. Douse every other living player to win alone at once. No sabotage; your tasks are fake.
role.arsonist.name: Arsonist
role.assassin.desc: An Impostor. In a meeting type /cmd guess <name> <role>: a correct guess kills the target, a wrong one kills you.
role.assassin.name: Assassin
role.bait.desc: Whoever kills you is forced to report your body immediately.
role.bait.name: Bait
role.evilhawk.desc: An Impostor who sees much further than a normal Impostor. Kills, vents and sabotages as usual.
role.evilhawk.name: Evil Hawk
role.evilnekomata.desc: An Impostor who kills normally. When you are voted out, one random player who voted for you dies with you.
role.evilnekomata.name: Evil Nekomata
role.jackal.desc: A neutral killer. You can kill anyone. Win by eliminating the Impostors and outnumbering the remaining crew.
role.jackal.name: Jackal
role.jackalfriends.desc: Jackal-side crewmate: you see the Jackal in blue, cannot kill, and win with the Jackal. Fake tasks.
role.jackalfriends.name: Jackal Friends
role.jester.desc: Neutral. You win alone if you get voted out. Your tasks are fake.
role.jester.name: Jester
role.lighter.desc: Your vision is wider than normal.
role.lighter.name: Lighter
role.lovers.desc: Lovers. You see a ♥ on your partner. If one of you dies the other dies too. Both alive when the game ends (or as the last 3 players) = you two win. Your tasks are fake.
role.lovers.name: Lovers
role.madhawk.desc: A crewmate on the Impostor team with much wider vision. You see Impostors in red but cannot kill. You win with the Impostors.
role.madhawk.name: Mad Hawk
role.madmate.desc: A crewmate on the Impostor team. You see Impostors in red but cannot kill. You win with the Impostors.
role.madmate.name: Madmate
role.madmayor.desc: A Madmate whose vote counts as several votes. You see Impostors in red but cannot kill; fake tasks.
role.madmayor.name: Mad Mayor
role.madstuntman.desc: A crewmate on the Impostor team. You see Impostors in red and cannot kill, but you survive the first few kill attempts (a vote still gets you). You win with the Impostors.
role.madstuntman.name: Mad Stuntman
role.mafia.desc: An Impostor who can only kill after all other Impostors are dead.
role.mafia.name: Mafia
role.mayor.desc: Your vote counts as several votes in meetings.
role.mayor.name: Mayor
role.none.name: None
role.opportunist.desc: Neutral. If you are alive when the game ends, you win too. Your tasks are fake.
role.opportunist.name: Opportunist
role.samurai.desc: An Impostor whose kill is a slash: your target dies, then everyone who was near you at that moment falls one after another. Long cooldown.
role.samurai.name: Samurai
role.serialkiller.desc: An Impostor with a very short kill cooldown. If you do not kill within the time limit after your last kill you die on the spot (the timer restarts with every kill and pauses during meetings). Can vent and sabotage.
role.serialkiller.name: Serial Killer
role.sheriff.desc: You have a kill button to shoot Impostors, the Jackal and the Arsonist (Mad-type roles and Jackal Friends by option). Shooting anyone else kills you instead. No venting or sabotage; your tasks are fake.
role.sheriff.name: Sheriff
role.snitch.desc: Finish all tasks to see Impostors in red, the Jackal in blue. When you are almost done, killers can see who you are.
role.snitch.name: Snitch
role.speedbooster.name: Speed Booster
role.terrorist.desc: Neutral. Finish all your tasks, then get killed or ejected to win alone.
role.terrorist.name: Terrorist
role.vampire.desc: An Impostor whose kill is a bite: the victim dies a few seconds later.
role.vampire.name: Vampire
role.witch.desc: An Impostor whose kill is a curse: everyone you cursed dies right after the next meeting. The curse fades if you are ejected or die.
role.witch.name: Witch
role.worshipper.desc: A crewmate on the Impostor team; you do not know who the Impostors are. Your kill button worships: the target becomes a Madmate (limited uses). Worshipping an Impostor kills you; after the last use the button only fails. No venting or sabotage; your tasks are fake.
role.worshipper.name: Worshipper
